10. In support of its case, the prosecution produced fifteen witnesses. However, according to the prosecution, the material witnesses having a direct bearing on the matter are Dr. Raheem Badshah (PW-9), who conducted the postmortem examination of the deceased Kholgi Shah, the complainant (PW-ll), and the Investigating Officer (PWl4).

ll. The complainant, Mir Wali Khan, appeared as PWll. He stated that the deceased, IGolgi Shah, was his brother. 13. A perusal of the evidence reflects that the complainant promptly reported the matter at KDA Hospital, Karak, narrating that on 24'07-2021 he and his late brother had gone to inspect their pressure pump, and at about 03:30 p.m. the accused suddenly appeared armed with a Kalashnikov and opened fire with the intention to kill them' His brother was hit and died on the spot, while he escaped unharmed. While appearing as PW-ll, the complainant remained firm on the material particulars of the case, and there is no reason to disbelieve his testimony, which stands corroborated by ocular, medical, and circumstantial evidence. The defence has not seriously disputed the x { - l0incident itself and has merely challenged the manner and mode of occurrence. No substantial challenge to the fact of the incident has been brought on record.

14. In cases involving a single accused, substitution is a rare phenomenon in offences under Section 302 PPC. The real culprits are seldom spared while innocent persons are falsely implicated. The complainant has assigned a clear motive of a property dispute, and there is nothing to suggest that the accused has been falsely or maliciously charged or that the actual culprit has been spared. The complainant and the deceased were real brothers residing in a joint household. In District Karak, due to absence of irrigation canals, people commonly irrigate their lands through wells and members ofjoint families work together in their fields. In these circumstances, the complainant's presence at the time and place ofoccurrence appears natural.

15. The prosecution evidence is consistent and free from doubts. Although the eyewitness was subjected to lengthy cross-examination yet his credibility remained intact, and his testimony on all material particulars could not be shaken. The FIR was lodged promptly, soon after the deceased was shifted to KDA Hospital, Karak, leaving no € rdom for deliberation or false implication' The record is also silent regarding any mala fide, i[ will, or animosity significant enough to falsely implicate the accused' 16. It is an admitted and undisputed fact on the record that at the time of spot inspection, the Investigating Officer recovered nine (09) crime empties from the place of occurence. The said empties were taken into possession through recovery memo Ex'PW-8/I. Thereafter, the same were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory @SL) for examination. As per the FSL report Ex'PZ, all the nine crime empties, marked C-l to C-9, were found to be of 7 '62 mm bore and it was opined by the expert that all the said empties were fired fiom one and the same7.62 mm bore weapon, which fully supports and corroborates the version of the complainant and establishes that a single assailant was involved in the commission of the offence' This fact further stands confirmed by subsequent events, when the appellant was arrested and the weapon of offence, i'e', a Kalashnikov rifle, was recovered from his possession' Regarding the said rccovery, a separate case bearing FIR No. 400 dated 15.07.2013, under sections 324,353 PPC and 15-AA, Police Station Karak, was registered against the appellant. Although the trial of the said case was conducted by the leamed Judicial Magistrate, yet it is evident from the record that the appellant was convicted and sentenced therein. The recovery memo and other relevant documents relating to the said recovery have been duly placed on the record of the instant murder case. After recovery' the said weapon along with recovered crime empties were again sent to the FSL for ballistic The FSL report conclusively proved that the crime empties recovered from the place of Wardat were fired from the same 7'62 mm (SMG) rifle bearing No. 66-56-l-14087892, which was recovered from the possession ofthe appellant. Thus, from all angles, the prosecution has successfully proved its case against the appellant through ocular as well as strong corroborative forensic evidence, leaving no room for doubt' The guilt of the appellant stands established beyond any shadow ofdoubt.

18. Upon re-appraisal of the entire evidence, it is concluded that the testimony of the complainant @W-11) remained consistent on all material particulars and stands coroborated by the medical and circumstantial evidence' There is nothing on record to suggest that the V:

substituted the accused for the real culprit. However, since the deceased received a single injury on a non-vital pan of the body, so we are constrained to hold that a mitigating circumstance does exist. Therefore, the conviction under Section 302-9 PPC and the sentence of death awarded to the appellant as Tazir is not sustainable. The appellant is, however, liable to conviction under Section 302(b) PPC, but the proper sentence in the circumstances is imprisonment for life. consequently, the death sentence is modified to imprisonment for life, and the death reference is declined' Benefit of Section 382-B Cr.P.C. is extended to the appellant-convict.
